people.descriptor: Diviner and Father of Guo Zixing
Son of Guo Zixing and Marshal
Daughter of Guo Zixing and Consort of Taizu
Prince of Shu, Son of Consort Hui
Prince of Gu, Son of Consort Hui
Prince of Dai, Son of Consort Hui
Claimed Kinsman of Prince of Chuyang
Mother of Han Lin'er and Empress Dowager
Former Yuan Official under Mao Gui

value.manner: uncertain; alternate report of drowning at Guabu

value.action: proclaimed emperor at Bo as Little Ming King

sourceDate.text: 毛貴已為其党趙均用所殺

units.zh: 郭子興 韓林兒
units.en: Guo Zixing; Han Lin'er
units.literal: Guo Zixing; Han Lin'er

units.zh: 郭子興
units.en: Guo Zixing
units.literal: Guo Zixing

units.zh: 郭子興，其先曹州人。
units.en: Guo Zixing's forebears were from Caozhou.
units.literal: Guo Zixing — his ancestors were men of Caozhou.

units.zh: 父郭公，少以日者術遊定遠，言禍福輒中。
units.en: His father, known as Master Guo, traveled in his youth through Dingyuan as a practitioner of calendrical divination; his predictions of good or ill fortune always proved accurate.
units.literal: His father, known as Master Guo, in youth wandered through Dingyuan practicing the art of day-selection; when he spoke of fortune or misfortune he was invariably right.

units.zh: 邑富人有瞽女無所歸，郭公乃娶之，家日益饒。
units.en: A wealthy townsman had a blind daughter with no place to turn; Master Guo married her, and the household grew steadily more prosperous.
units.literal: A wealthy man in the district had a blind daughter with nowhere to go; Master Guo then married her, and the family daily grew richer.

units.zh: 生三子，子興其仲出。
units.en: She bore three sons; Zixing was the middle son.
units.literal: She bore three sons; Zixing was born of her as the second son.

units.zh: 始生，郭公卜之吉。
units.en: When he was born, Master Guo divined an auspicious outcome.
units.literal: At his birth, Master Guo divined that it was auspicious.

units.zh: 及長，任俠，喜賓客。
units.en: As he matured, he lived by the code of the knight-errant and loved to entertain guests.
units.literal: When he grew up, he was chivalrous and bold, and delighted in hosting guests.

units.zh: 會元政亂，子興散家資，椎牛釃酒，與壯士結納。
units.en: With the Yuan regime falling into chaos, Zixing spent the family fortune—slaughtering oxen and broaching wine—to win over bold followers.
units.literal: As it happened the Yuan government was in disorder; Zixing dispersed the family wealth, slaughtered oxen and poured wine, and formed bonds with stalwart men.

units.zh: 至正十二年春，集少年數千人，襲據濠州。
units.en: In the spring of the Zhizheng twelfth year (1352), he rallied several thousand young men and seized Haozhou in a sudden attack.
units.literal: In the spring of the twelfth year of Zhizheng, he gathered several thousand youths and seized Haozhou by surprise.

units.zh: 太祖往從之。
units.en: The future Hongwu Emperor went to join his cause.
units.literal: The Founding Emperor went to join him.

units.zh: 門者疑其諜，執以告子興。
units.en: A sentry took him for a spy, arrested him, and reported to Zixing.
units.literal: The gatekeeper suspected him of being a spy, seized him, and reported this to Zixing.

units.zh: 子興奇太祖狀貌，解縛與語，收帳下。
units.en: Zixing was struck by the newcomer's striking appearance; he had him unbound, spoke with him, and took him into his service.
units.literal: Zixing was struck by the Founding Emperor's unusual appearance; he loosed his bonds and spoke with him, and took him into his personal following.

units.zh: 為十夫長，數從戰有功。
units.en: He was appointed chief of ten; he fought again and again and won distinction.
units.literal: He was made leader of ten men; repeatedly in battle he followed and achieved merit.

units.zh: 子興喜，其次妻小張夫人亦指目太祖曰：「此異人也。」
units.en: Zixing was delighted, and his second wife, the younger Lady Zhang, gestured toward the future emperor and said, "This is no ordinary man."
units.literal: Zixing was pleased; his second wife, Lady Zhang the Younger, also pointing at the Founding Emperor said: "This is an extraordinary man."

units.zh: 乃妻以所撫馬公女，是為孝慈高皇后。
units.en: He then gave him in marriage the daughter he had raised—the daughter of Master Ma—who became Empress Xiaoci the Great.
units.literal: He then gave him in marriage the daughter whom he had raised, the daughter of Master Ma — this was Empress Xiaoci the Great.

units.zh: 始，子興同起事者孫德崖等四人，與子興而五，各稱元帥不相下。
units.en: At first Zixing and four fellow insurgents—Sun Deya among them—together with Zixing made five commanders, each styling himself marshal and refusing to yield to the others.
units.literal: At the beginning, Zixing and the four who had risen with him—Sun Deya and others—with Zixing made five; each called himself marshal and would not yield to the others.

units.zh: 四人者粗而戇，日剽掠，子興意輕之。
units.en: The four were crude and rash, plundering every day; Zixing looked down on them.
units.literal: The four were coarse and dull-witted; daily they plundered; Zixing in his mind held them in contempt.

units.zh: 四人不悅，合謀傾子興。
units.en: The four resented this and plotted together to bring Zixing down.
units.literal: The four were displeased and together plotted to overthrow Zixing.

units.zh: 子興以是多家居不視事。
units.en: Zixing therefore spent much of his time at home and neglected command duties.
units.literal: Because of this Zixing often stayed at home and did not attend to affairs.

units.zh: 太祖乘閑說曰：「彼日益合，我益離，久之必為所制。」
units.en: When he had a moment alone with Zixing, the future emperor warned, "They are drawing closer together while we drift apart; in time they will control us."
units.literal: The Founding Emperor, seizing an idle moment, urged: "They day by day grow more united; we day by day grow more isolated; in time we shall surely be controlled by them."

units.zh: 子興不能從也。
units.en: Zixing would not heed him.
units.literal: Zixing could not follow this advice.

units.zh: 元師破徐州，徐帥彭大、趙均用帥餘眾奔濠。
units.en: Yuan armies took Xu Prefecture; the Xu commanders Peng Da and Zhao Junyong led their surviving forces to Haozhou.
units.literal: Yuan forces broke Xu Prefecture; the Xu commanders Peng Da and Zhao Junyong led the remaining troops in flight to Haozhou.

units.zh: 德崖等以其故盜魁有名，乃共推奉之，使居己上。
units.en: Because Peng and Zhao were famous former bandit leaders, Deya and the others jointly elevated them above their own ranks.
units.literal: Deya and the others, because they were former bandit chiefs of renown, thereupon jointly promoted and honored them, placing them above themselves.

units.zh: 大有智數，子興與相厚而薄均用。
units.en: Peng Da was shrewd and capable; Zixing favored him while slighting Zhao Junyong.
units.literal: Da was greatly intelligent and resourceful; Zixing was thick friends with him but slighted Junyong.

units.zh: 於是德崖等譖諸均用曰：「子興知有彭將軍耳，不知有將軍也。」
units.en: Deya and his allies then slandered Zixing to Junyong: "Zixing knows only General Peng—he acts as if you did not exist."
units.literal: Thereupon Deya and the others slandered Zixing to Junyong, saying: "Zixing knows only General Peng; he does not know there is a General [you]."

units.zh: 均用怒，乘間執子興，幽諸德崖家。
units.en: Enraged, Junyong seized Zixing at an opportune moment and imprisoned him in Deya's house.
units.literal: Junyong was angry; seizing an opportunity he seized Zixing and confined him in Deya's house.

units.zh: 太祖自他部歸，大驚，急帥子興二子訴於大。
units.en: The future emperor returned from another command, was alarmed, and hurried to Peng Da with Zixing's two sons to appeal for help.
units.literal: The Founding Emperor returned from another division, was greatly alarmed, and urgently led Zixing's two sons to plead with Da.

units.zh: 大曰：「吾在，孰敢魚肉而翁者！」
units.en: Peng Da said, "As long as I am here, who would dare abuse your father-in-law!"
units.literal: Da said: "While I am here, who dares treat your father-in-law like fish on the chopping block!"

units.zh: 與太祖偕詣德崖家，破械出子興，挾之歸。
units.en: He went with the future emperor to Deya's house, broke Zixing's chains, and escorted him back.
units.literal: Together with the Founding Emperor he went to Deya's house, broke the fetters, brought Zixing out, and escorted him home.

units.zh: 元師圍濠州，乃釋故憾，共城守五閱月。
units.en: When Yuan forces besieged Haozhou, the factions set aside old grudges and held the city together for five months.
units.literal: Yuan troops besieged Haozhou; they then released old grievances and jointly defended the city for five months.

units.zh: 圍解，大、均用皆自稱王，而子興及德崖等為元帥如故。
units.en: After the siege lifted, Peng Da and Zhao Junyong each proclaimed himself king, while Zixing, Deya, and the others retained the title of marshal.
units.literal: When the siege was lifted, Da and Junyong each declared himself king, while Zixing and Deya and the others remained marshals as before.

units.zh: 未幾，大死，子早住領其眾。
units.en: Before long Peng Da died, and his son Zao Zhuo inherited his troops.
units.literal: Before long Da died; his son Zao Zhuo took command of his forces.

units.zh: 均用專狠益甚，挾子興攻盱眙、泗州，將害之。
units.en: Zhao Junyong grew ever more vicious; he forced Zixing to attack Xuyi and Sizhou, plotting to destroy him in the process.
units.literal: Junyong grew ever more tyrannical and cruel; he pressured Zixing to attack Xuyi and Sizhou, intending to harm him.

units.zh: 太祖已取滁，乃遣人說均用曰：「大王窮迫時，郭公開門延納，德至厚也。
units.en: By then the future emperor had taken Chuzhou; he sent an envoy to Zhao Junyong: "When you were desperate, Lord Guo welcomed you in—his kindness was profound.
units.literal: The Founding Emperor had already taken Chu; he then sent someone to persuade Junyong, saying: "When Your Highness was in desperate straits, Lord Guo opened his gates and received you—his virtue was exceedingly great.

units.zh: 大王不能報，反聽細人言圖之，自剪羽翼，失豪傑心，竊為大王不取。
units.en: Yet instead of repaying him, you heed petty advisers plotting his ruin—you are cutting away your own wings and forfeiting the loyalty of great men; I cannot believe this serves you well.
units.literal: Your Highness cannot repay this, yet instead listens to petty men's words plotting against him—you cut your own wings, lose the hearts of heroes; I venture to say this is not what Your Highness should do.

units.zh: 且其部曲猶眾，殺之得無悔乎？」
units.en: Besides, his followers are still numerous—will you not regret killing him?"
units.literal: Moreover his following is still numerous—if you kill him, will you not regret it?"

units.zh: 均用聞太祖兵甚盛，心憚之，太祖又使人賂其左右，子興用是得免，乃將其所部萬余就太祖于滁。
units.en: Junyong, hearing how strong the future emperor's forces had become, was afraid; the future emperor also bribed his confidants, and Zixing was spared. He then brought his division of more than ten thousand men to join the future emperor at Chuzhou.
units.literal: Junyong heard that the Founding Emperor's troops were very strong and feared him in his heart; the Founding Emperor also sent men to bribe those around him, and by this means Zixing was spared; he then led his division of more than ten thousand to join the Founding Emperor at Chu.

units.zh: 子興為人梟悍善鬥，而性悻直少容。
units.en: Zixing was fierce and warlike, yet obstinate and unforgiving by nature.
units.literal: Zixing as a man was fierce and bold, skilled in fighting, yet by nature obstinate and straight, with little forbearance.

units.zh: 方事急，輒從太祖謀議，親信如左右手。
units.en: In a crisis he relied on the future emperor's counsel and trusted him as he would his own hands.
units.literal: When affairs were urgent he would follow the Founding Emperor in counsel; he trusted him as his own left and right hands.

units.zh: 事解，即信讒疏太祖。
units.en: Once the danger passed, he believed slanders and distanced himself from the future emperor.
units.literal: When the crisis passed, he at once believed slanders and kept the Founding Emperor at a distance.

units.zh: 太祖左右任事者悉召之去，稍奪太祖兵柄。
units.en: He recalled all the future emperor's trusted lieutenants and gradually stripped him of command.
units.literal: All those around the Founding Emperor who handled affairs were summoned away; he gradually stripped the Founding Emperor of military authority.

units.zh: 太祖事子興愈謹。
units.en: The future emperor served Zixing with ever greater deference.
units.literal: The Founding Emperor served Zixing with ever greater care.

units.zh: 將士有所獻，孝慈皇后輒以貽子興妻。
units.en: Whenever his officers brought gifts, Empress Xiaoci would pass them on to Zixing's wife.
units.literal: When officers and soldiers had offerings, Empress Xiaoci would promptly give them to Zixing's wife.

units.zh: 子興至滁，欲據以自王。
units.en: After Zixing arrived at Chuzhou, he wanted to seize it and proclaim himself king.
units.literal: When Zixing reached Chu, he wished to hold it and make himself king.

units.zh: 太祖曰：「滁四面皆山，舟楫商旅不通，非可旦夕安者也。」
units.en: The future emperor said, "Chuzhou is ringed by mountains; no boats or trade routes reach it—it is no place to build a lasting base overnight."
units.literal: The Founding Emperor said: "Chu is surrounded on all sides by mountains; boats, carts, merchants, and travelers cannot pass through—it is not a place where one can settle in a day or a night."

units.zh: 子興乃已。
units.en: Zixing abandoned the plan.
units.literal: Zixing then stopped.

units.zh: 及取和州，子興命太祖統諸將守其地。
units.en: After He Prefecture was captured, Zixing put the future emperor in command of the garrison there.
units.literal: When He Prefecture was taken, Zixing ordered the Founding Emperor to command the generals in holding that territory.

units.zh: 德崖饑，就食和境，求駐軍城中，太祖納之。
units.en: Deya, short of provisions, entered He territory to forage and asked to quarter his troops in the city; the future emperor agreed.
units.literal: Deya was starving; he came to He territory to seek food and asked to station troops inside the city; the Founding Emperor admitted them.

units.zh: 有讒於子興者。
units.en: Someone slandered the future emperor to Zixing.
units.literal: Someone slandered the Founding Emperor to Zixing.

units.zh: 子興夜至和，太祖來謁，子興怒甚，不與語。
units.en: Zixing arrived at He by night; when the future emperor came to pay his respects, Zixing was furious and refused to speak with him.
units.literal: Zixing came by night to He; the Founding Emperor came to pay his respects; Zixing was very angry and would not speak with him.

units.zh: 太祖曰：「德崖嘗困公，宜為備。」
units.en: The future emperor said, "Deya once had you at his mercy—you should be on guard."
units.literal: The Founding Emperor said: "Deya once brought you to straits—you should take precautions."

units.zh: 子興默然。
units.en: Zixing said nothing.
units.literal: Zixing was silent.

units.zh: 德崖聞子興至，謀引去。
units.en: Hearing that Zixing had arrived, Deya planned to withdraw.
units.literal: Deya heard that Zixing had come and plotted to withdraw.

units.zh: 前營已發，德崖方留視後軍，而其軍與子興軍鬥，多死者。
units.en: The vanguard had already marched out; Deya had stayed behind with the rearguard, but his troops clashed with Zixing's, and many were killed on both sides.
units.literal: The vanguard had already set out; Deya had only remained to oversee the rear guard, but his army and Zixing's army fought, and many died.

units.zh: 子興執德崖，太祖亦為德崖軍所執。
units.en: Zixing captured Deya, but Deya's men seized the future emperor in turn.
units.literal: Zixing seized Deya; the Founding Emperor was also seized by Deya's army.

units.zh: 子興聞之，大驚，立遣徐達往代太祖，縱德崖還。
units.en: Alarmed, Zixing sent Xu Da to take the future emperor's place as hostage and released Deya.
units.literal: When Zixing heard of this he was greatly alarmed; he immediately sent Xu Da to replace the Founding Emperor and released Deya to return.

units.zh: 德崖軍釋太祖，達亦脫歸。
units.en: Deya's men released the future emperor, and Xu Da returned safely as well.
units.literal: Deya's army released the Founding Emperor; Da also escaped and returned.

units.zh: 子興憾德崖甚，將甘心焉，以太祖故強釋之，邑邑不樂。
units.en: Zixing hated Deya and was ready to kill him, but released him only for the future emperor's sake—yet he remained bitter and dissatisfied.
units.literal: Zixing resented Deya deeply and was about to take satisfaction in killing him; because of the Founding Emperor he forced himself to release him, yet was discontented and unhappy.

units.zh: 未幾，發病卒，歸葬滁州。
units.en: Before long he fell ill and died; his body was brought back for burial at Chuzhou.
units.literal: Before long he fell ill and died; he was buried back at Chuzhou.

units.zh: 子興三子。
units.en: Zixing had three sons.
units.literal: Zixing had three sons.

units.zh: 長子前戰死，次天敘、天爵。
units.en: The eldest had died in battle earlier; the survivors were Tianxu and Tianjue.
units.literal: The eldest son had died earlier in battle; the next were Tianxu and Tianjue.

units.zh: 子興死，韓林兒檄天敘為都元帥，張天祐及太祖副之。
units.en: After Zixing's death, Han Lin'er appointed Tianxu commander-in-chief, with Zhang Tianyou and the future emperor as his deputies.
units.literal: When Zixing died, Han Lin'er by edict appointed Tianxu as commander-in-chief, with Zhang Tianyou and the Founding Emperor as his deputies.

units.zh: 天祐，子興婦弟也。
units.en: Tianyou was the younger brother of Zixing's wife.
units.literal: Tianyou was Zixing's wife's younger brother.

units.zh: 太祖渡江，天敘、天祐引兵攻集慶，陳野先叛，俱被殺。
units.en: When the future emperor crossed the Yangzi, Tianxu and Tianyou led an attack on Jiqing; Chen Yexian turned traitor, and both were killed.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor crossed the Yangzi, Tianxu and Tianyou led troops to attack Jiqing; Chen Yexian rebelled, and both were killed.

units.zh: 林兒復以天爵為中書右丞。
units.en: Lin'er then appointed Tianjue Right Chancellor of the Secretariat.
units.literal: Lin'er again appointed Tianjue Right Chancellor of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 已而太祖為平章政事。
units.en: Before long the future emperor became Vice Director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: Before long the Founding Emperor became Vice Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 天爵失職怨望，久之謀不利於太祖，誅死，子興後遂絕。
units.en: Deposed and resentful, Tianjue eventually plotted against the future emperor and was executed; with him, Zixing's male line ended.
units.literal: Tianjue, having lost his post, harbored resentment; after a long while he plotted against the Founding Emperor and was executed; Zixing's line thus came to an end.

units.zh: 有一女，小張夫人出者，事太祖為惠妃，生蜀、穀、代三王。
units.en: He had a daughter by the younger Lady Zhang who became Consort Hui to the future emperor and bore the princes of Shu, Gu, and Dai.
units.literal: He had one daughter, born of the younger Lady Zhang, who served the Founding Emperor as Consort Hui and bore the three princes of Shu, Gu, and Dai.

units.zh: 洪武三年追封子興為滁陽王，詔有司建廟，用中牢祀，復其鄰宥氏，世世守王墓。
units.en: In Hongwu year 3 (1370), Zixing was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Chuyang; the court built a temple and offered the middle sacrifice; the You clan of his neighborhood was restored to guard the tomb in perpetuity.
units.literal: In the third year of Hongwu he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Chuyang; an edict ordered the officials to build a temple and sacrifice with the middle offering; his neighbor the You clan was restored, generation after generation to guard the prince's tomb.

units.zh: 十六年，太祖手書子興事蹟，命太常丞張來儀文其碑。
units.en: In year 16 (1383), the Hongwu Emperor wrote Zixing's life story in his own hand and commissioned Zhang Laiyi, Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices, to compose the stele inscription.
units.literal: In the sixteenth year, the Founding Emperor in his own hand wrote Zixing's deeds and ordered the Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices Zhang Laiyi to compose the text for his stele.

units.zh: 滁人郭老舍者，宣德中以滁陽王親，朝京師。
units.en: A Chu townsman named Guo Laoshe, claiming to be kin to the Prince of Chuyang, presented himself at court during the Xuande reign (1426–1435).
units.literal: A man of Chu named Guo Laoshe, claiming kinship with the Prince of Chuyang, in the Xuande reign came to the capital to pay court.

units.zh: 弘治中，有郭琥自言四世祖老舍，滁陽王第四子，予冠帶奉祀。
units.en: During Hongzhi (1488–1505), a Guo Hu claimed his fourth-generation ancestor Laoshe was the prince's fourth son and was granted official rank to conduct sacrifices.
units.literal: In the Hongzhi reign, a Guo Hu claimed that his fourth-generation ancestor Laoshi was the Prince of Chuyang's fourth son; he was granted cap and belt to perform sacrifices.

units.zh: 已，為宥氏所訐。
units.en: Later the You clan denounced him.
units.literal: Later he was impeached by the You clan.

units.zh: 禮官言：「滁陽王祀典，太祖所定，曰無後，廟碑昭然，老舍非滁陽王子。」
units.en: The Board of Rites ruled: "The Hongwu Emperor established these rites and declared the prince had no heirs; the temple stele is explicit—Laoshe was not his son."
units.literal: The ritual officials said: "The sacrificial rites for the Prince of Chuyang were fixed by the Founding Emperor, who declared there were no descendants; the temple stele is clear—Laoshi was not a son of the Prince of Chuyang."

units.zh: 奪奉祀。
units.en: His right to conduct sacrifices was revoked.
units.literal: His right to perform sacrifices was revoked.

units.zh: 韓林兒
units.en: Han Lin'er
units.literal: Han Lin'er

units.zh: 韓林兒，欒城人，或言李氏子也。
units.en: Han Lin'er was from Luancheng; some said he was actually a son of the Li clan.
units.literal: Han Lin'er was a man of Luancheng; some say he was a son of the Li clan.

units.zh: 其先世以白蓮會燒香惑眾，謫徙永年。
units.en: His ancestors, who had used the White Lotus Society to gather followers through incense rites, were exiled to Yongnian.
units.literal: His forebears, through the White Lotus Society burning incense to delude the masses, were banished and relocated to Yongnian.

units.zh: 元末，林兒父山童鼓妖言，謂「天下當大亂，彌勒佛下生」。
units.en: Late in the Yuan, Lin'er's father Shantong preached sedition: "The realm will soon be in chaos; Maitreya Buddha is coming down to earth."
units.literal: At the end of the Yuan, Lin'er's father Shantong spread demonic talk, saying: "The realm is about to fall into great disorder; Maitreya Buddha will descend to be born."

units.zh: 河南、江、淮間愚民多信之。
units.en: Many simple folk between Henan and the Yangzi–Huai region believed him.
units.literal: Among the foolish commoners between Henan and the Yangzi and Huai regions many believed this.

units.zh: 潁州人劉福通與其党杜遵道、羅文素、盛文鬱等復言「山童，宋徽宗八世孫，當主中國」。
units.en: Liu Futong of Yingzhou and his followers—Du Zundao, Luo Wensu, Sheng Wenyu, and others—again declared, "Shantong is the eighth-generation descendant of Song Huizong and should rule China."
units.literal: Liu Futong of Ying Prefecture and his partisans Du Zundao, Luo Wensu, Sheng Wenyu, and others again declared: "Shantong is the eighth-generation descendant of Emperor Huizong of Song; he should rule China."

units.zh: 乃殺白馬黑牛，誓告天地，謀起兵，以紅巾為號。
units.en: They sacrificed a white horse and a black ox, swore an oath to Heaven and Earth, plotted rebellion, and took the red turban as their emblem.
units.literal: They then slaughtered a white horse and a black ox, swore before Heaven and Earth, plotted to raise troops, and took the red turban as their sign.

units.zh: 至正十一年五月，事覺，福通等遽入潁州反，而山童為吏所捕誅。
units.en: In the fifth month of Zhizheng 11 (1351), the plot was exposed; Futong and his men rose immediately in Yingzhou, while officials captured and executed Shantong.
units.literal: In the fifth month of the eleventh year of Zhizheng the plot was discovered; Futong and the others hastily entered Ying Prefecture in rebellion, while Shantong was seized by officials and executed.

units.zh: 林兒與母楊氏逃武安山中。
units.en: Lin'er and his mother, Lady Yang, fled into the Wu'an mountains.
units.literal: Lin'er and his mother, Lady Yang, fled into the mountains of Wu'an.

units.zh: 福通據硃皋，破羅山、上蔡、真陽、確山，犯葉、舞陽，陷汝寧、光、息，眾至十余萬，元兵不能禦。
units.en: Futong seized Zhugao and stormed Luoshan, Shangcai, Zhenyang, Queshan, Ye, and Wuyang, capturing Runing, Guang, and Xi; his forces swelled past a hundred thousand, and Yuan armies could not stop him.
units.literal: Futong held Zhugao, broke Luoshan, Shangcai, Zhenyang, and Queshan, raided Ye and Wuyang, and took Runing, Guang, and Xi; his forces reached more than a hundred thousand, and Yuan troops could not resist.

units.zh: 時徐壽輝等起蘄、黃，布王三、孟海馬等起湘、漢，芝麻李起豐、沛，而郭子興亦據濠應之。
units.en: Meanwhile Xu Shouhui rose in Qi and Huang, Bu Wangsan and Meng Haima in Xiang and Han, Sesame Li in Feng and Pei, and Guo Zixing seized Haozhou in sympathy.
units.literal: At that time Xu Shouhui and others rose in Qi and Huang; Bu Wangsan, Meng Haima, and others rose in Xiang and Han; Sesame Li rose in Feng and Pei; and Guo Zixing also held Haozhou in response.

units.zh: 時皆謂之「紅軍」，亦稱「香軍」。
units.en: They were all called the "Red Army," also known as the "Incense Army."
units.literal: At the time all were called the "Red Army," also styled the "Incense Army."

units.zh: 十五年二月，福通物色林兒，得諸碭山夾河；
units.en: In the second month of year 15 (1355), Futong found Lin'er between the rivers at Dangshan;
units.literal: In the second month of the fifteenth year, Futong sought out Lin'er and found him between the rivers at Dangshan;

units.zh: 迎至亳，僭稱皇帝，又號小明王，建國曰宋，建元龍鳳。
units.en: brought him to Bo, where Lin'er was proclaimed emperor and styled Little Ming King; the state was named Song and the era Longfeng.
units.literal: he welcomed him to Bo, where he presumptuously styled himself emperor, also took the title Little Ming King, established a state called Song, and adopted the era name Longfeng.

units.zh: 拆鹿邑太清宮材，治宮闕於亳。
units.en: Timber from the Taiqing Palace at Luyi was torn down to build palaces at Bo.
units.literal: Timber from the Taiqing Palace at Luyi was dismantled to build palaces at Bo.

units.zh: 尊楊氏為皇太后，遵道、文郁為丞相，福通、文素平章政事，劉六知樞密院事。
units.en: Lady Yang was honored as Empress Dowager; Zundao and Wenyu became chancellors; Futong and Wensu, Vice Directors of the Secretariat; Liu Liu, Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
units.literal: Lady Yang was honored as Empress Dowager; Zundao and Wenyu were made chancellors; Futong and Wensu were Vice Directors of the Secretariat; Liu Liu was made Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

units.zh: 劉六者，福通弟也。
units.en: Liu Liu was Futong's younger brother.
units.literal: Liu Liu was Futong's younger brother.

units.zh: 遵道寵用事。
units.en: Zundao held favor and wielded power.
units.literal: Zundao was favored and monopolized power.

units.zh: 福通嫉之，陰命甲士撾殺遵道，自為丞相，加太保，事權一歸福通。
units.en: Futong, jealous, had armed men beat Zundao to death; he took the chancellorship himself, added the title Grand Guardian, and concentrated all power in his own hands.
units.literal: Futong envied him; secretly he ordered armored soldiers to beat Zundao to death; he himself became chancellor, was additionally made Grand Guardian, and all authority returned to Futong alone.

units.zh: 既而元師大敗福通于太康，進圍亳，福通挾林兒走安豐。
units.en: Soon Yuan forces routed Futong at Taikang and besieged Bo; Futong fled with Lin'er to Anfeng.
units.literal: Before long Yuan troops heavily defeated Futong at Taikang and advanced to besiege Bo; Futong took Lin'er and fled to Anfeng.

units.zh: 未幾，兵復盛，遣其黨分道略地。
units.en: Before long their armies revived; he sent his followers on separate campaigns to seize territory.
units.literal: Before long their forces flourished again; he sent his partisans by separate routes to seize territory.

units.zh: 十七年，李武、崔德陷商州，遂破武關以圖關中，而毛貴陷膠、萊、益都、濱州，山東郡邑多下。
units.en: In year 17 (1357), Li Wu and Cui De took Shangzhou and broke through Wuguan toward Guanzhong, while Mao Gui seized Jiao, Lai, Yidu, and Binzhou; most of Shandong fell.
units.literal: In the seventeenth year, Li Wu and Cui De took Shang Prefecture, then broke Wuguan Pass to aim at Guanzhong; meanwhile Mao Gui took Jiao, Lai, Yidu, and Bin Prefecture, and many commanderies and districts of Shandong fell.

units.zh: 是年六月，福通帥眾攻汴梁，且分軍三道：關先生、破頭潘、馮長舅、沙劉二、王士誠趨晉、冀；
units.en: That June, Futong led his forces against Bianliang and divided them into three columns: Master Guan, Potou Pan, Feng Changjiu, Shaliu Er, and Wang Shicheng marched on Shanxi and Hebei;
units.literal: In the sixth month of that year Futong led his masses to attack Bianliang, and moreover divided his army into three routes: Master Guan, Potou Pan, Feng Changjiu, Shaliu Er, and Wang Shicheng pressed toward Jin and Ji;

units.zh: 白不信、大刀敖、李喜喜趨關中；
units.en: Bai Buxin, Dadao Ao, and Li Xixi marched on Guanzhong;
units.literal: Bai Buxin, Dadao Ao, and Li Xixi pressed toward Guanzhong;

units.zh: 毛貴出山東北犯。
units.en: Mao Gui marched out of Shandong and struck northeast.
units.literal: Mao Gui came out from Shandong and raided northeastward.

units.zh: 勢銳甚。
units.en: His momentum was fierce.
units.literal: His momentum was exceedingly sharp.

units.zh: 田豐者，元鎮守黃河義兵萬戶也，叛附福通，陷濟寧，尋敗走。
units.en: Tian Feng had been a Yuan commander of militia along the Yellow River; he defected to Futong, seized Jining, but was soon defeated and driven off.
units.literal: Tian Feng was a Yuan ten-thousand-household commander of righteous troops guarding the Yellow River; he rebelled and joined Futong, took Jining, and soon was defeated and fled.

units.zh: 其秋，福通兵陷大名，遂自曹、濮陷衛輝。
units.en: That autumn Futong's forces took Daming, then advanced from Cao and Pu to seize Weihui.
units.literal: That autumn Futong's troops took Daming, then from Cao and Pu took Weihui.

units.zh: 白不信、大刀敖、李喜喜陷興元，遂入鳳翔，屢為察罕帖木兒、李思齊所破，走入蜀。
units.en: Bai Buxin, Dadao Ao, and Li Xixi took Xingyuan and entered Fengxiang, but were repeatedly defeated by Chaghan Temür and Li Siqi and driven into Sichuan.
units.literal: Bai Buxin, Dadao Ao, and Li Xixi took Xingyuan, then entered Fengxiang; repeatedly they were broken by Chaghan Temür and Li Siqi and fled into Shu.

units.zh: 十八年，田豐復陷東平、濟寧、東昌、益都、廣平、順德。
units.en: In year 18 (1358), Tian Feng recaptured Dongping, Jining, Dongchang, Yidu, Guangping, and Shunde.
units.literal: In the eighteenth year Tian Feng again took Dongping, Jining, Dongchang, Yidu, Guangping, and Shunde.

units.zh: 毛貴亦數敗元兵，陷清、滄，據長蘆鎮，尋陷濟南；
units.en: Mao Gui also defeated Yuan forces several times, seized Qing and Cang, held Changlu, and soon took Jinan;
units.literal: Mao Gui also repeatedly defeated Yuan troops, took Qing and Cang, held Changlu Town, and soon took Jinan;

units.zh: 益引兵北，殺宣慰使董搏霄于南皮，陷薊州，犯漷州，略柳林以逼大都。
units.en: then pushed north, killed the Pacification Commissioner Dong Boxiao at Nanpi, took Jizhou, raided Huozhou, and swept through Liulin toward Dadu.
units.literal: further he led troops north, killed the Pacification Commissioner Dong Boxiao at Nanpi, took Jizhou, raided Huozhou, and swept through Liulin to press upon Dadu.

units.zh: 順帝征四方兵入衛，議欲遷都避其鋒，大臣諫乃止。
units.en: Emperor Shundi summoned troops from all quarters to defend the capital; courtiers debated relocating the capital to escape Mao's advance, but ministers dissuaded him.
units.literal: Emperor Shundi summoned troops from the four quarters to guard the capital; there was discussion of moving the capital to avoid his edge, but ministers remonstrated and it stopped.

units.zh: 貴旋被元兵擊敗，還據濟南。
units.en: Mao Gui was soon beaten back and retreated to Jinan.
units.literal: Gui was soon defeated by Yuan troops and returned to hold Jinan.

units.zh: 而福通出沒河南北，五月攻下汴梁，守將竹貞遁去，遂迎林兒都焉。
units.en: Meanwhile Futong ranged across Henan; in the fifth month he took Bianliang, the defender Zhuzhen fled, and he installed Lin'er as his capital there.
units.literal: Meanwhile Futong ranged north and south of the Henan region; in the fifth month he attacked and took Bianliang; the defending general Zhuzhen fled, and he thereupon welcomed Lin'er to make it his capital.

units.zh: 關先生、破頭潘等又分其軍為二，一出絳州，一出沁州。
units.en: Master Guan, Potou Pan, and the others split their forces again—one column from Jiangzhou, one from Qinzhou.
units.literal: Master Guan, Potou Pan, and the others again divided their army in two—one column out from Jiang Prefecture, one from Qin Prefecture.

units.zh: 逾太行，破遼、潞，遂陷冀寧；
units.en: They crossed the Taihang Mountains, overran Liao and Lu, and seized Jining;
units.literal: They crossed the Taihang range, broke Liao and Lu, and then took Jining;

units.zh: 攻保定不克，陷完州，掠大同、興和塞外諸郡，至陷上都，毀諸宮殿，轉掠遼陽，抵高麗。
units.en: they failed to take Baoding but seized Wanzhou, raided Datong, Xinghe, and frontier districts, captured Shangdu and destroyed its palaces, then swept through Liaoyang as far as Goryeo.
units.literal: they attacked Baoding but could not take it, took Wan Prefecture, plundered Datong, Xinghe, and the outer districts beyond the passes, even took Shangdu, destroyed the palaces, turned to plunder Liaoyang, and reached Goryeo.

units.zh: 十九年陷遼陽，殺懿州路總管呂震。
units.en: In year 19 (1359) they took Liaoyang and killed Lü Zhen, the Yizhou circuit intendant.
units.literal: In the nineteenth year they took Liaoyang and killed Lü Zhen, circuit intendant of Yizhou.

units.zh: 順帝以上都宮闕盡廢，自此不復北巡。
units.en: With Shangdu's palaces in ruins, Emperor Shundi never toured the north again.
units.literal: Because the palaces at Shangdu were wholly ruined, Emperor Shundi from this time never again toured north.

units.zh: 李喜喜餘黨復陷寧夏，略靈武諸邊地。
units.en: Li Xixi's remaining followers seized Ningxia and raided the Lingwu frontier.
units.literal: The remnant bands of Li Xixi again took Ningxia and overran the borderlands around Lingwu.

units.zh: 是時承平久，川郡皆無守備。
units.en: After long peace, inland prefectures had no defenses.
units.literal: At this time peace had lasted long; the inland prefectures all lacked defenses.

units.zh: 長吏聞賊來，輒棄城遁，以故所至無不摧破。
units.en: Local officials fled at the first rumor of rebels, so the Red Army swept through almost unopposed.
units.literal: When senior officials heard rebels were coming they would abandon their cities and flee; for this reason wherever the rebels went nothing failed to be smashed and broken.

units.zh: 然林兒本起盜賊，無大志，又聽命福通，徒擁虛名。
units.en: Yet Lin'er was a bandit chieftain at heart, without grand ambition, and obeyed Futong—holding only a hollow title.
units.literal: Yet Lin'er had originally risen from banditry and had no great ambition; moreover he obeyed Futong's orders and merely held an empty name.

units.zh: 諸將在外者率不遵約束，所過焚劫，至啖老弱為糧，且皆福通故等夷，福通亦不能制。
units.en: Generals in the field ignored discipline, burning and looting wherever they went—even eating the old and weak for food; as Futong's former equals, they obeyed him no better than he could command them.
units.literal: The generals abroad for the most part did not obey discipline; wherever they passed they burned and plundered, even eating the old and weak for provisions; moreover they were all Futong's former equals, and Futong also could not control them.

units.zh: 兵雖盛，威令不行。
units.en: For all their numbers, they had no real authority.
units.literal: Though their troops were strong, authority and orders did not prevail.

units.zh: 數攻下城邑，元兵亦數從其後復之，不能守。
units.en: They took cities again and again, but Yuan forces recaptured them just as often—they could not hold what they seized.
units.literal: Repeatedly they attacked and took cities and districts, but Yuan troops also repeatedly recovered them from behind—they could not hold them.

units.zh: 惟毛貴稍有智略。
units.en: Only Mao Gui showed any real strategic sense.
units.literal: Only Mao Gui had some intelligence and strategy.

units.zh: 其破濟南也，立賓興院，選用元故官姬宗周等分守諸路。
units.en: When he took Jinan, he established an academy for recruiting scholars and appointed former Yuan officials such as Ji Zongzhou to govern the various circuits.
units.literal: When he took Jinan he established a Guest and Promotion Academy and selected former Yuan officials such as Ji Zongzhou to guard the various routes in turn.

units.zh: 又於萊州立屯田三百六十所，每屯相距三十里，造挽運大車百輛，凡官民田十取其二。
units.en: He established three hundred sixty military farms in Lai, spaced thirty li apart, built a hundred large transport carts, and levied a tax of two-tenths on all public and private land.
units.literal: He also established three hundred sixty military colonies at Lai, each colony thirty li apart, built a hundred large transport carts for hauling, and from all official and private fields took two parts in ten.

units.zh: 多所規畫，故得據山東者三年。
units.en: With such planning he held Shandong for three years.
units.literal: He planned many such measures; therefore he was able to hold Shandong for three years.

units.zh: 及察罕帖木兒數破賊，盡復關、隴，是年五月大發秦、晉之師會汴城下，屯杏花營，諸軍環城而壘。
units.en: After Chaghan Temür had repeatedly defeated the rebels and recovered Guanzhong and Longyou, in the fifth month of that year he massed Qin and Jin armies below Bianliang, encamped at Apricot Blossom Camp, and ringed the city with siege works.
units.literal: When Chaghan Temür had repeatedly broken the rebels and wholly recovered Guan and Long, in the fifth month of that year he greatly dispatched Qin and Jin armies to assemble below Bian city, encamped at Apricot Blossom Camp, and the various armies ringed the city with fortifications.

units.zh: 林兒兵出戰輒敗，嬰城守百餘日，食將盡。
units.en: Lin'er's forces sallied out and were beaten each time; after more than a hundred days of siege, food was nearly gone.
units.literal: Lin'er's troops sallied forth to battle and were repeatedly defeated; they clung to the city in defense for more than a hundred days, and provisions were nearly exhausted.

units.zh: 福通計無所出，挾林兒從百騎開東門遁還安豐，後宮官屬子女及符璽印章寶貨盡沒於察罕。
units.en: Futong, at his wits' end, fled through the east gate with Lin'er and a hundred horsemen back to Anfeng; the harem, officials, children, seals, and treasures all fell to Chaghan.
units.literal: Futong, with no plan left, took Lin'er with a hundred horsemen, opened the east gate, and fled back to Anfeng; the harem, officials, sons and daughters, seals, tallies, and treasures all fell into Chaghan's hands.

units.zh: 時毛貴已為其党趙均用所殺，有續繼祖者，又殺均用，所部自相攻擊。
units.en: By then Mao Gui had been killed by his follower Zhao Junyong; Xu Jizu then killed Junyong, and their factions turned on one another.
units.literal: By then Mao Gui had already been killed by his partisan Zhao Junyong; a certain Xu Jizu then killed Junyong in turn, and their divisions attacked one another.

units.zh: 獨田豐據東平，勢稍強。
units.en: Only Tian Feng held Dongping, and his position was somewhat stronger.
units.literal: Only Tian Feng held Dongping, and his power was somewhat stronger.

units.zh: 二十年，關先生等陷大寧，復犯上都。
units.en: In year 20 (1360), Master Guan and his men took Daning and raided Shangdu again.
units.literal: In the twentieth year Master Guan and the others took Daning and again raided Shangdu.

units.zh: 田豐陷保定，元遣使招之，被殺。
units.en: Tian Feng took Baoding; when the Yuan sent envoys to negotiate, he had them killed.
units.literal: Tian Feng took Baoding; the Yuan sent envoys to summon him, and he had them killed.

units.zh: 王士誠又躪晉、冀。
units.en: Wang Shicheng overran Shanxi and Hebei again.
units.literal: Wang Shicheng again trampled Jin and Ji.

units.zh: 元將孛羅敗之於台州，遂入東平與豐合。
units.en: The Yuan general Boluo defeated him at Taizhou; he then entered Dongping and joined Tian Feng.
units.literal: The Yuan general Boluo defeated him at Taizhou; he then entered Dongping and joined forces with Feng.

units.zh: 福通嘗責李武、崔德逗撓，將罪之。
units.en: Futong once blamed Li Wu and Cui De for foot-dragging and was about to punish them.
units.literal: Futong once blamed Li Wu and Cui De for delay and shirking and was about to punish them.

units.zh: 二十一年夏，兩人叛去，降于李思齊。
units.en: In the summer of year 21 (1361), the two defected and surrendered to Li Siqi.
units.literal: In the summer of the twenty-first year the two rebelled and left, surrendering to Li Siqi.

units.zh: 時李喜喜、關先生等東西轉戰，已多走死，餘黨自高麗還寇上都，孛羅復擊降之。
units.en: By then Li Xixi, Master Guan, and others had fought across the realm; many had died in flight; remnant bands returning from Goryeo raided Shangdu, and Boluo defeated and accepted their surrender.
units.literal: By then Li Xixi, Master Guan, and the others had fought east and west; many had fled and died; remnant bands returning from Goryeo raided Shangdu, and Boluo again attacked and forced their surrender.

units.zh: 而察罕既取汴梁，遂遣子擴廓討東平，脅降田豐、王士誠，乘勝定山東。
units.en: After Chaghan took Bianliang, he sent his son Köke Temür against Dongping, forced Tian Feng and Wang Shicheng to submit, and pacified Shandong in the wake of victory.
units.literal: After Chaghan had taken Bianliang, he then sent his son Köke Temür to campaign against Dongping, coerced the surrender of Tian Feng and Wang Shicheng, and following victory pacified Shandong.

units.zh: 惟陳猱頭者，獨守益都不下，與福通遙為聲援。
units.en: Only Chen Yaotou held out in Yidu, giving distant support to Futong.
units.literal: Only Chen Yaotou alone held Yidu and would not submit, giving distant mutual support with Futong.

units.zh: 二十二年六月，豐、士誠乘閑刺殺察罕，入益都。
units.en: In the sixth month of year 22 (1362), Feng and Shicheng assassinated Chaghan when his guard was down and entered Yidu.
units.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-second year Feng and Shicheng seized an opening and assassinated Chaghan, then entered Yidu.

units.zh: 元以兵柄付擴廓，圍城數重，猱頭等告急。
units.en: The Yuan gave military command to Köke Temür, who laid siege in concentric rings; Yaotou sent urgent appeals for aid.
units.literal: The Yuan entrusted military authority to Köke Temür, who besieged the city in many rings; Yaotou and the others sent urgent appeals for help.

units.zh: 福通自安豐引兵赴援，遇元師于火星埠，大敗走還。
units.en: Futong marched from Anfeng to relieve the siege but was routed at Mars Ford and driven back.
units.literal: Futong led troops from Anfeng to the rescue; he met Yuan forces at Mars Ford, was heavily defeated, and fled back.

units.zh: 元兵急攻益都，穴地道以入，殺豐、士城，而械送猱頭于京師，林兒勢大窘。
units.en: Yuan forces stormed Yidu, tunneled into the city, killed Feng and Shicheng, and sent Yaotou in chains to the capital; Lin'er's position collapsed.
units.literal: Yuan troops pressed the attack on Yidu, tunneled underground to enter, killed Feng and Shicheng, and sent Yaotou in fetters to the capital; Lin'er's position became greatly straitened.

units.zh: 明年，張士誠將呂珍圍安豐，林兒告急于太祖。
units.en: The following year Zhang Shicheng's general Lü Zhen besieged Anfeng, and Lin'er appealed to the future emperor for help.
units.literal: The next year Zhang Shicheng's general Lü Zhen besieged Anfeng; Lin'er appealed in urgency to the Founding Emperor.

units.zh: 太祖曰：「安豐破則士誠益強。」
units.en: The future emperor said, "If Anfeng falls, Zhang Shicheng will grow stronger still."
units.literal: The Founding Emperor said: "If Anfeng falls, Shicheng will grow stronger still."

units.zh: 遂親帥師往救，而珍已入城殺福通。
units.en: He led the army personally to the rescue, but Lü Zhen had already entered the city and killed Futong.
units.literal: He thereupon personally led troops to the rescue, but Zhen had already entered the city and killed Futong.

units.zh: 太祖擊走珍，以林兒歸，居之滁州。
units.en: The future emperor drove Lü Zhen off, brought Lin'er back, and installed him at Chuzhou.
units.literal: The Founding Emperor struck and drove Zhen away, brought Lin'er back with him, and lodged him at Chuzhou.

units.zh: 明年，太祖為吳王。
units.en: The following year the future emperor became King of Wu.
units.literal: The next year the Founding Emperor became King of Wu.

units.zh: 又二年，林兒卒。
units.en: Two years later Lin'er died.
units.literal: Two years later Lin'er died.

units.zh: 或曰太祖命廖永忠迎林兒歸應天，至瓜步，覆舟沉于江雲。
units.en: Some say the Hongwu Emperor ordered Liao Yongzhong to escort Lin'er to Yingtian; at Guabu the boat capsized and he drowned in the river—or so it is said.
units.literal: Some say the Founding Emperor ordered Liao Yongzhong to welcome Lin'er back to Yingtian; at Guabu the boat capsized and he sank in the river—so it is said.

units.zh: 初，太祖駐和陽，郭子興卒，林兒牒子興子天敘為都元帥，張天祐為右副元帥，太祖為左副元帥。
units.en: Early on, while the future emperor was stationed at Heyang, Guo Zixing died; Lin'er issued an edict appointing Zixing's son Tianxu commander-in-chief, Zhang Tianyou right deputy marshal, and the future emperor left deputy marshal.
units.literal: At first, when the Founding Emperor was stationed at Heyang, Guo Zixing died; Lin'er issued an edict appointing Zixing's son Tianxu as commander-in-chief, Zhang Tianyou as right deputy marshal, and the Founding Emperor as left deputy marshal.

units.zh: 時太祖以孤軍保一城，而林兒稱宋後，四方回應，遂用其年號以令軍中。
units.en: At that time the future emperor held a lone city with a small force; Lin'er claimed to be heir to the Song, the realm answered from all sides, and he adopted Lin'er's era name to command his troops.
units.literal: At that time the Founding Emperor held a single city with isolated troops; Lin'er claimed descent from the Song, responses came from all quarters, and he therefore adopted Lin'er's era name to command the army.

units.zh: 林兒歿，始以明年為吳元年。
units.en: After Lin'er's death, the next year was reckoned as the first year of Wu.
units.literal: When Lin'er died, the following year was taken as Wu year 1.

units.zh: 其年，遣大將軍定中原，順帝北走，距林兒亡僅歲餘。
units.en: That year he sent a great general to pacify the Central Plains; Emperor Shundi fled north, barely more than a year after Lin'er died.
units.literal: That year he dispatched a great general to pacify the Central Plains; Emperor Shundi fled north—only a little over a year after Lin'er's death.

units.zh: 林兒僭號凡十二年。
units.en: Lin'er's usurped reign lasted twelve years in all.
units.literal: Lin'er's presumptuous title lasted twelve years in all.

units.zh: 贊曰：元之末季，群雄蜂起。
units.en: The encomium says: In the Yuan's final years, rival warlords rose everywhere.
units.literal: The encomium says: In the late age of the Yuan, rival heroes swarmed forth like bees.

units.zh: 子興據有濠州，地偏勢弱。
units.en: Zixing held Haozhou—a remote post with little strength.
units.literal: Zixing held Haozhou—his territory remote and his power weak.

units.zh: 然有明基業，實肇于滁陽一旅。
units.en: Yet the Ming enterprise truly began with that single brigade at Chuyang.
units.literal: Yet the foundation of the Ming enterprise in truth began with that single brigade at Chuyang.

units.zh: 子興之封王祀廟，食報久長，良有以也。
units.en: That Zixing was enfeoffed as a prince, given a temple, and honored for generations was well deserved.
units.literal: Zixing's enfeoffment as prince, his temple sacrifices, and his long-lasting reward in offerings—there was good reason for all this.

units.zh: 林兒橫據中原，縱兵蹂躪，蔽遮江、淮十有餘年。
units.en: Lin'er dominated the central plains, his armies ravaging the land and shielding the Yangzi–Huai region for more than a decade.
units.literal: Lin'er sprawled across the central plains, let his troops rampage and trample, and screened the Yangzi and Huai for more than ten years.

units.zh: 太祖得以從容締造者，藉其力焉。
units.en: The future emperor was able to build his realm at leisure in part because Lin'er absorbed his rivals' attention.
units.literal: That the Founding Emperor was able at leisure to forge and establish his rule owed something to Lin'er's strength.

units.zh: 帝王之興，必有先驅者資之以成其業，夫豈偶然哉！
units.en: When an emperor rises, forerunners must pave the way for his success—how could it be mere chance!
units.literal: When an emperor or king rises, there must be forerunners who supply the means to accomplish his enterprise—how could this be mere chance!
